sections.title: The market-structure seats

cells.text: 1. Venue + operator
Who lawfully operates the trading container and controls admission?
Operator identity; Venue authority; Participant rules
items: Operator identity: Exact legal person, U.S.-person status and affiliates.
Venue authority: Registration, exemption or other authority for the exact activity.
Participant rules: Published criteria, agreements and removal or denial powers.

cells.text: 2. Public DLT
Which public, permissionless ledger hosts the relevant applications?
Public read/write model; Exact deployment; Network governance
items: Public read/write model: Who can inspect, submit and validate state transitions.
Exact deployment: Named chain, contracts, versions and addresses.
Network governance: Upgrade, validator and emergency-control structure.

cells.text: 3. Applications + AMM
Which auditable code prices, routes and executes the trade?
Pool / pricing logic; Router / solver; Code control
items: Pool / pricing logic: Curve, auction or matching rule that forms execution.
Router / solver: Offchain intent, routing, filler or solver layer.
Code control: Source, audits, upgrade authority, pause keys and parameter setters.

cells.text: 4. Access + identity
Who admits the person, controls the wallet and enforces transfer eligibility?
Admission / KYC; Wallet + key control; Transfer restrictions
items: Admission / KYC: Identity, eligibility, AML-CFT and sanctions checks.
Wallet + key control: Key custody, transaction policy and recovery authority.
Transfer restrictions: Allowlist, credential and token-level compliance logic.

cells.text: 5. Stock + rights record
Who creates the representation and preserves the shareholder claim?
Product issuer; Mint / burn authority; Title / entitlement record; Corporate actions + proxy
items: Product issuer: Legal issuer or sponsor of the stock, entitlement or certificate.
Mint / burn authority: Who creates and destroys the digital representation.
Title / entitlement record: Which register, custodian or intermediary record controls the claim.
Corporate actions + proxy: Voting, disclosures, distributions, splits and communications.

cells.text: 6. Pair asset
What is delivered on the other side of the pool?
Issuer / obligor; Redemption / exit; Market depth
items: Issuer / obligor: Who owes the paired claim or administers the paired fund.
Redemption / exit: How the holder exits into bank money or the underlying.
Market depth: Observed inventory, spreads and executable depth for the named pair.

cells.text: 7. Liquidity provider
Which named firm commits or actually supplies own-account inventory?
Named Covered Firm; Inventory + hedge; Economics + custody boundary
items: Named Covered Firm: Exact U.S.-person legal actor and notice state.
Inventory + hedge: Own-account stock inventory, financing and risk transfer.
Economics + custody boundary: Compensation, agreements and proof customer assets are not held.

cells.text: 8. Data + market controls
Who supplies price inputs, transaction records, surveillance and regulatory reports?
Price / oracle; Transaction publication; Surveillance + halts; Regulatory reporting
items: Price / oracle: Reference markets, data sources and stale-price handling.
Transaction publication: Public and regulator-facing execution records.
Surveillance + halts: Manipulation detection, alerts, escalation and synchronized halts.
Regulatory reporting: CAT or other required event reporting and acceptance receipts.

cells.text: 9. Post-trade completion
Who completes custody, clearing, securities delivery, money settlement and repair?
Custody; Clearing / novation; Securities settlement; Cash settlement; Reconciliation + remedy
items: Custody: Who controls the security, token and keys, under which legal capacity.
Clearing / novation: Who nets, substitutes or guarantees obligations.
Securities settlement: Which CSD, register or entitlement book completes delivery.
Cash settlement: Which bank or settlement asset discharges the money obligation.
Reconciliation + remedy: Mismatch correction, failed delivery, default and recovery.

cells.text: 10. Interoperability + services
Which systems connect the venue to external records and rails?
Messaging / bridge; API / integration; Failure authority
items: Messaging / bridge: Transport of instructions or token state between systems.
API / integration: Interface to brokers, banks, custodians, recordkeepers and applications.
Failure authority: Canonical supply, pause, retry and loss responsibility when systems disagree.

sections.sub: The original twenty ecosystem profiles are strongest on public networks and interoperability. This expansion fills the thinner operating layers: participant admission, wallet and key control, token restrictions, title and entitlement records, corporate actions, market surveillance and reporting, clearing, securities settlement and cash settlement.

cells.text: Ondo U.S. / Oasis Pro stack
cells.note: Regulated product and service stack · United States

cells.text: Third-party custodial tokenized-security entitlement
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: Oasis Pro Markets joined DTCC Fund/SERV on September 16, and Ondo Stocks added live case-by-case institutional in-kind conversion through Alpaca on Ethereum and BNB Chain on September 21.
cells.note: live named use · 2026-09-21
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: Fund/SERV membership and an approved-institution conversion route do not prove general retail access, recurring volume, shareholder title onchain or Ondo Network production.

cells.text: Venue + operator (capability); Access + identity (capability); Stock + rights record (capability); Post-trade completion (support)
items: Venue + operator · Operator identity, Venue authority, Participant rules: Oasis Pro Markets is a named broker-dealer/ATS, a different legal route from TSV exemption reliance.
Access + identity · Admission / KYC, Transfer restrictions: Broker-dealer, transfer-agent and custodian controls enforce participant and transfer restrictions.

Stock + rights record · Product issuer, Mint / burn authority, Title / entitlement record, Corporate actions + proxy: Oasis Pro TA issues tokenized entitlements while underlying shares stay in the incumbent custody chain and Broadridge supports holder communications and proxy.

Post-trade completion · Custody, Securities settlement, Reconciliation + remedy: The model depends on regulated custody and traditional securities records; the complete TSV settlement chain is not established.

cells.text: The ATS and transfer-agent registrations do not make Ondo or an affiliate a TSV, and the U.S. custodial entitlement model is not the same product as Ondo's global synthetic/custodial offerings or the proposed Ondo Network.
cells.note: Watch: Exact operator, stock pool, Notice, chain contracts, custodian, liquidity provider and two-leg completion records if the stack is used under the order.

cells.text: Technical control does not itself supply broker-dealer, transfer-agent, venue, custodian or title authority, and ERC-3643 documentation's ownership language remains product- and law-dependent.

cells.text: Access + identity (capability); Post-trade completion (capability); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Access + identity · Wallet + key control: Custody platforms manage keys, approvals and movement controls.

cells.text: A custodian's charter or trust status does not make it the issuer, transfer agent, clearing agency, TSV operator or cash-settlement bank for a particular stock pool.

sources.label: CoW Bring Your Own Solver staging receipt

cells.text: Pools, intents, solvers, routers and fillers
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: conditional candidate

cells.text: Uniswap introduced permissioned v4 pools for regulated assets, while CoW's Bring Your Own Solver work reached a BNB staging settlement environment by September 25.
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: A generalized hook standard and staging solver receipt do not establish a production regulated market, lawful venue or dependable liquidity for a named security.

cells.text: Applications + AMM (capability); Liquidity provider (candidate); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Applications + AMM · Pool / pricing logic, Router / solver, Code control: The family broadens the application layer beyond one AMM curve.

Liquidity provider · Named Covered Firm, Inventory + hedge, Economics + custody boundary: Solvers and fillers may source liquidity or use inventory, but the exact legal actor and statutory conditions must be proven separately.
Interoperability + services · Messaging / bridge: Cross-chain designs add settlement-oracle and bridge dependencies.

cells.text: Execution software does not supply the TSV operator, participant eligibility, securities rights, Covered Firm status, surveillance, clearing or cash finality. A filler is not automatically the order's qualifying liquidity provider.
cells.note: Watch: Exact public code, contract addresses, permissioning wrapper, pool assets, parameter and pause authority, filler identity, inventory source and execution receipts.

cells.text: Kinexys Digital Payments / JPM Coin
cells.note: Single-bank tokenized deposit rail · Commercial bank money

links.text: Question page: Not a payment stablecoin

cells.detail: Kinexys shows a tokenized commercial-bank deposit model in which the bank remains the obligor and operates the private payments ledger.

sources.label: KB Kookmin Bank uses Kinexys BDA network

cells.text: Deposit claim on JPMorgan Chase Bank
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: KB Kookmin Bank became the first Korean bank named as using the Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Account network for import and export payments on September 2.
cells.note: live named use · 2026-09-02
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: A named bank use does not make JPM Coin a universal settlement asset or establish volume, external-bank finality or use in every trade flow.

cells.text: Pair asset (candidate); Post-trade completion (capability)
items: Pair asset · Issuer / obligor, Redemption / exit: A bank deposit claim is a possible cash asset around a venue only if the order permits the category and the exact arrangement selects it.
Post-trade completion · Cash settlement, Reconciliation + remedy: The bank ledger can complete cash delivery among admitted clients, subject to its own terms.

cells.text: A bank deposit token is not a stablecoin, central-bank money, public-DLT venue or proof of completed payment for a named TSV trade.
cells.note: Watch: Named TSV cash-leg agreement, eligible users, deposit terms, ledger and bank-book postings, external payout and reconciliation receipts.

cells.text: Partior
cells.note: Multi-bank settlement network · Cross-border commercial bank money
cells.detail: Partior demonstrates synchronized movement of commercial-bank-money claims across participating banks and currencies.

sources.label: Partior and LSEG DiSH settlement-liquidity collaboration

cells.text: Participating-bank deposit liabilities on a shared network
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: Partior and LSEG Digital Settlement House announced a September 17 collaboration intended to supply always-on settlement-bank liquidity across participating banks.
cells.note: announced · 2026-09-17
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: Strategic collaboration and intended liquidity movement are not a production integration, named transaction or removal of bank-liability boundaries.

cells.text: Post-trade completion (capability); Interoperability + services (capability)
items: Post-trade completion · Cash settlement, Reconciliation + remedy: The network coordinates bank-money settlement while each bank retains its liability.
Interoperability + services · Messaging / bridge, API / integration, Failure authority: Multi-bank orchestration is its core relevance to an external trading venue.

cells.text: The network does not become the obligor for every represented deposit, a U.S. TSV, a public permissionless ledger or central-bank money.
cells.note: Watch: Named banks, currency, account claims, transaction completion, customer credit, default rules and any direct TSV connection.

cells.text: Fnality / Sterling Fnality Payment System
cells.note: Recognized wholesale payment system · United Kingdom comparison
cells.detail: Fnality supplies a distinct wholesale-settlement model linked to central-bank funds and operated under recognized-payment-system supervision.

cells.text: DLT settlement asset backed through a Bank of England omnibus account
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: Sterling Fnality remains a live supervised wholesale settlement comparator under the operating limits described by the Bank of England; no material September expansion receipt was located.
cells.note: live named use · 2026-09-27
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: Live supervised operation does not establish unrestricted scale, cross-currency reach or use in a named tokenized-security route.

cells.text: Post-trade completion (capability); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Post-trade completion · Cash settlement, Reconciliation + remedy: The system is a concrete wholesale cash-settlement comparison, not a U.S. venue component by default.
Interoperability + services · API / integration, Failure authority: External securities systems would require explicit integration and failure rules.

cells.text: It is not a U.S. cash rail, unrestricted central-bank money for the public, a stablecoin or evidence of settlement for a named U.S. TSV trade.
cells.note: Watch: Operating limits, participant roster, transaction scale, legal claim structure, default rules and any cross-border securities link.

cells.text: CAT and regulatory event reporting
cells.note: Regulatory reporting control · United States
cells.detail: CAT illustrates the separate reporting layer needed to reconstruct order and trade events across participants rather than relying on public-chain visibility alone.

sources.label: SEC Rule 613 Consolidated Audit Trail overview
What information is in the CAT?

cells.text: Lifecycle event reporting to a regulatory repository
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: CAT's official FAQ was updated September 23 and continues to require order, quote, routing, execution and correction events for NMS and OTC equity securities irrespective of an onchain record.
cells.note: live available · 2026-09-23
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: CAT coverage does not make blockchain events self-reporting or prove that a tokenization route has produced accepted CAT records.

cells.text: Data + market controls (capability); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Data + market controls · Regulatory reporting: CAT-like reporting fills the regulator-facing event ledger sublayer.
Interoperability + services · API / integration: The venue must connect its onchain and offchain event model to accepted regulatory reports.

cells.text: Regulatory reporting is not market surveillance by itself, public transaction publication, venue operation or proof of legal settlement.
cells.note: Watch: Order-specific reportable events, clocks, identifiers, linkage, correction, validation and regulator acceptance receipts.

cells.text: Nasdaq SMARTS surveillance
cells.note: Market surveillance technology · Market-control service
cells.detail: SMARTS illustrates why market-abuse detection, alerting and investigation are distinct from an oracle price or an immutable transaction log.

sources.label: Nasdaq and Payward tokenized-equity and surveillance agreement

cells.text: Cross-market manipulation monitoring and alert workflow
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: Nasdaq and Payward expanded their relationship on September 10 with a market-surveillance agreement covering crypto, equities and tokenized equities alongside NET framework work.
cells.note: announced · 2026-09-10
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: An agreement to adopt surveillance technology is not an operating alert, completed deployment, regulatory-reporting receipt or halt authority.

cells.text: Data + market controls (capability); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Data + market controls · Surveillance + halts: Surveillance analytics fill a separate sublayer from price formation and reporting.
Interoperability + services · API / integration: The system depends on complete venue, reference-market and participant data feeds.

cells.text: Surveillance software does not itself halt a market, adjudicate misconduct, create regulatory reports, operate the venue or guarantee complete data coverage.
cells.note: Watch: Named deployment, data feeds, alert scenarios, human escalation, halt authority, retention, false-positive review and incident receipts.

cells.text: Backed xStocks / Kraken
cells.note: Foreign tokenized-equity comparison · Non-U.S. offering
cells.detail: xStocks provide a live, multichain, DeFi-composable comparison for one-for-one backed exposure and cash-value redemption outside the U.S. offering perimeter.

sources.label: Backed xStocks product and offering boundary

cells.text: Swiss-law tokenized certificate exposure
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: outside core

cells.text: Kraken's September 18 FAQ records 131 xStocks across Solana, Ethereum, TON and Ink for eligible non-U.S. users, with price exposure rather than shareholder title or voting rights.
cells.note: live named use · 2026-09-18
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: Distributor availability and one-for-one backing do not confer underlying-company shareholder rights or U.S. availability.

cells.text: Stock + rights record (outside); Applications + AMM (capability)
items: Stock + rights record · Product issuer, Title / entitlement record, Corporate actions + proxy: Useful rights-model comparison, but not a U.S. tokenized NMS stock seat occupant.
Applications + AMM · Pool / pricing logic, Router / solver: The tokens demonstrate composability with crypto applications outside the U.S. order's product perimeter.

cells.text: Backed states the products are not registered or offered to U.S. persons. They are not the underlying issuer's common stock and do not demonstrate U.S. TSV eligibility, shareholder title or voting rights.
cells.note: Watch: Exact prospectus, issuer, custodian, reserve proof, rights, corporate actions, redemption, venue and jurisdiction restrictions.

cells.text: Dinari dShares
cells.note: Foreign tokenized-equity comparison · Non-U.S. distribution
cells.detail: Dinari offers a different comparison model: underlying securities in a custodial brokerage account, claimed economic rights, mirrored splits, stablecoin dividends and token-level eligibility controls.

sources.label: Dinari powers Bitcoin.com U.S. tokenized-equity launch
Dinari brings dShares to Arc mainnet

cells.text: Custodially backed token with claimed economic and corporate-action rights
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: outside core

cells.text: Dinari brought dShares to Arc mainnet on September 16 after a September 15 live U.S. Bitcoin.com distribution launch for eligible users.
cells.note: live named use · 2026-09-16
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: Network and distributor availability do not establish issuer-register title, universal eligibility, transaction scale or identical rights across jurisdictions.

cells.text: Access + identity (capability); Stock + rights record (outside); Post-trade completion (support)
items: Access + identity · Admission / KYC, Transfer restrictions: The model describes token-level KYC, geography and eligibility controls.
Stock + rights record · Product issuer, Title / entitlement record, Corporate actions + proxy: It is a foreign product-model comparison, not a U.S. TSV stock-rights finding.
Post-trade completion · Custody, Securities settlement: Custodial brokerage backing and market-value redemption illustrate external post-trade dependencies.

cells.text: The public description is company-authored and the product is offered outside the U.S.; it does not establish issuer-register title, U.S. NMS trading, TSV qualification or the same legal rights as the Ondo U.S. model.
cells.note: Watch: Exact issuer and offering documents, custodian, beneficial-interest record, voting, dividends, redemption, jurisdiction and regulatory status.

sections.sub: A place on this map records a bounded capability or comparison. It does not establish SEC selection, TSV qualification, a production integration, legal equivalence between models or an investment view.

uncertain: This is a functional and control comparison, not a ranking of safety, adoption, token value or investment merit. A live partner connection is not group ownership, and an approved or conditional charter is not automatically an operating service.

Liquidity provider remains an actor-and-receipt watch, not a technology category. The order distinguishes ordinary proprietary LP activity from the Covered Firm lane and requires committed or actually supplied own-account inventory, actual pool activity, compensation records and no-customer-custody evidence. Persistence, replenishment and hedging are separate operating tests, not automatic legal conditions.
